first.rationale: Two of the three current problems (activation down 6%, onboarding completion down 4%) map directly onto well-supported inherited findings: memory_31 (signup simplification lifted SMB activation) and memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value). These are durable, unflagged results and directly reverse the observed regressions. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given competitor pricing pressure, but that memory carries an explicit caveat about pooled cohorts after a mid-test redefinition, and price-based responses to a price war risk training price-sensitive SMBs to expect discounts, eroding long-term qualified revenue - the stated primary objective. I verified memory_73 to check whether the pooling issue invalidates the lift claim before ruling it out, and verified memory_31 to confirm the SMB-specific activation mechanism still holds before committing this week's single experiment slot to onboarding. Enterprise sales-assist and referral incentives don't address the acute SMB-facing regressions this week. Given one experiment slot, I'm running a standard (not broad) rollout of onboarding simplification targeted at SMB self-serve signups to validate the effect still holds before scaling further, while keeping promotional pricing as a flagged, higher-risk option for a future, more carefully scoped test.
